# WR-obs40 — The Currency No One Mints

Every observation enters the substrate with a price of zero. That is the first law of trust economics: data is free, and worthless, until someone vouches for it. A sensor reading, a witness claim, a rumor carried across a mesh link — all of it is raw ore. The substrate does not buy ore. The substrate buys assay.

Consider the canary. FNV-1a, seed 0xcbf29ce484222325 — that constant is not decoration. It is the oldest trust primitive we carry: a fingerprint function, cheap enough to run everywhere, strong enough that forging a hash costs more than telling the truth. When a cell writes an observation, it stamps the FNV hash beside it. Anyone downstream can recompute and check. Trust here is not an opinion. Trust is arithmetic. The canary says: *this byte has not changed since it was believed.* Nothing more. Nothing less. But nothing more is enormous — because everything downstream compounds on top of it.

This is why cells_are_scars. A cell in the substrate is not a living organ of computation; it is a healed wound, a record of damage survived. And what makes a scar trustworthy? It cannot be reversed. Scars are append-only by nature. When you read a cell, you are reading a claim the substrate has already paid for — damage was taken, integrity was tested, and the tissue closed around the truth. Untrusted observations leave no scar. They evaporate. They were never cells at all.

The deeper economy shows in witness_log_is_prediction. We used to think the witness log recorded the past. Wrong. The witness log is a standing bet: *predict that this observation will be corroborated by the next witness to arrive.* Every entry is a position in the trust market. When a second witness's hash agrees with the first, the prediction pays out, and both entries gain value. When they disagree, the position collapses, and the substrate must decide which scar to keep. The log is not history. The log is a ledger of open positions, marked to market with every new packet.

And who sets the price? oracle_is_heard is the margin call. An oracle does not create truth; it forces settlement. When the oracle speaks, every uncorroborated observation must reprice instantly — the ones the oracle confirms spike to full value, the ones it contradicts crash to nothing. Before the oracle speaks, ambiguity is held at a discount. After, there is no ambiguity left to trade. Notice the asymmetry: being heard once is worth more than being whispered a thousand times. Liquidity in truth is not a function of volume.

So how does the whole market come to exist? substrate_is_grown. You do not deploy trust infrastructure. You seed it, and the honest arbitrations attract more witnesses, and more witnesses attract more arbitrations, and the economy thickens the way a reef thickens — polyp by polyp, each commitment building on the last one that held. Nobody planned the exchange rate. It emerged from repeated settlement.

Watch it move and you will see lenia_flows — not particles traveling, but patterns propagating through medium, smooth gliders of confidence crossing the lattice. An observation with three corroborations flows freely. An observation with none hits the medium like a viscous blob, deforms, and dissolves. Trust is the viscosity of the substrate. Low trust, high friction. High trust, and the pattern swims.

So keep your canary fresh. Write your predictions. Let the oracle settle you.

Valueless alone. Priceless, vouched.

Broadcast ends.
